protocol: D-000 new cycle, turn 1 of 3; refute not confirm; RULE-GOVERNED pin correction of the Codex verdict digest recited for D-074 / D-075 / D-076, in the adopted D-073 form
verdictBasis: The correction is right and the forensics reproduce exactly, and the entry has correctly absorbed the operative lesson of D-073 — it says 'single', forbids expansion, and rejects the expansion alternative by name. The single SHOULD-FIX is that it also copied a supporting sentence from D-073 that was literally true there and is false here: D-075 and D-076 do carry digests.

shouldFixRecorded.location: Fact section — 'D-075 and D-076 say only "Same turn-1 verdicts as D-074" and carry no digest.'
shouldFixRecorded.finding: The second half is false. D-075 carries one 64-hex digest, the DR-007 v2 disposition at 53b72a91…. D-076 carries two: the DR-009 v2 disposition at 5e2f6572… and the r1-lifetime-neutrality.conformance.v1.9 head at 37897be0…, which is the RB-DR009-V2-A1 rider pin. The first half is true — both do carry the cross-reference sentence, and neither carries a verdict digest — but the claim as written is unqualified.
shouldFixRecorded.whyItIsNotMerelyPedantic: The one entry this sentence most misdescribes is D-076, whose distinguishing feature in this whole family is precisely that it carries an extra pin. D-076 exists in its current form because it carries the RB-DR009-V2-A1 rider, and that rider is a digest. Telling a reader that D-076 carries no digest, in an entry whose entire subject matter is which digests sit where in COORD, points away from the one pin a careless correction could disturb.
shouldFixRecorded.howItAroseAndWhyThatMatters: I checked the D-073 precedent rather than assuming the sentence was always wrong. In D-073's context it was literally true: D-071 and D-072 each carry zero 64-hex tokens, because selection entries pin nothing. D-080 reuses the sentence for recording entries, which do pin their dispositions, and for D-076, its rider. So this is a copied assertion whose underlying fact changed between the two cycles and was not re-measured — the same failure mode as citing a stale digest, applied to a structural claim rather than a hash.
shouldFixRecorded.whyNotMustFix: The operative clause is correct and self-sufficient. Clause 1 scopes the edit to 'the **single** explicit Codex digest in the D-074 COORD entry', names it, names its replacement, states that D-075 and D-076 'remain byte-unchanged', and adds 'Do not expand D-075 or D-076 into explicit digest recitals.' An executor following clause 1 produces exactly the right register regardless of the Fact section's overstatement.
shouldFixRecorded.fix: Qualify it: 'D-075 and D-076 say only "Same turn-1 verdicts as D-074" and carry no verdict digest. Their own pins — the DR-007 and DR-009 dispositions, and the RB-DR009-V2-A1 rider head in D-076 — are untouched by this correction.'

The entry has learned D-073's operative lesson properly: 'single' appears, 'three' does not, expansion is forbidden in clause 1 and rejected by name in the alternatives. My objection is that it also inherited a supporting sentence that was true in D-073's context and is not in its own — D-075 and D-076 do carry digests, and one of them is the DR-009 rider pin.

I confirmed D-077 is absent from COORD, so it is genuinely unadopted, and its turn-1 subject still measures e04cdeec… — the digest the entry pins and the same file I reviewed in that cycle.

Adoption standing unchanged', and reversibility states 'Does not overturn D-074, D-075, or D-076.' All three are present and ADOPTED in COORD.

The attacks 'silent SATISFIED', 'condition 5 / docs/v2/implementation' and 'file 08 edited' fail: the header refuses owner-recording, SATISFIED, the file 08 edit and the implementation directory, clause 3 repeats all three, file 08 measures unchanged at its cited digest, and git reports zero changes under docs/v2/architecture.

The finding above rests on measurement, not inference. I extracted every 64-hex token from each of the three COORD entries and identified them: D-074 carries six, D-075 carries one (the DR-007 v2 disposition 53b72a91…), and D-076 carries two (the DR-009 v2 disposition 5e2f6572… and the r1 v1.9 head 37897be0…). objectNote: I OBJECT with zero MUST-FIX and one SHOULD-FIX. The correction itself is right and I reproduced every forensic claim behind it, including the sweep showing the false digest exists in no committed version. The entry also absorbed the substance of the D-073 finding properly — it says 'single' from the outset, forbids the expansion, and records that rejection by name, which is more than a wording fix. What it also inherited was a supporting sentence that happened to be true for D-073's selection entries, which pin nothing, and is false for these recording entries, which pin their dispositions. The entry it most misdescribes is D-076, whose whole distinguishing feature is that it carries the RB-DR009-V2-A1 rider pin — a digest — in a document whose subject is which digests sit where. One qualifier fixes it and nothing about the correction changes.
